core.title: Plan batched or fused work only where it preserves logical results and boundaries
core.given: a plan has repeated homogeneous operations, database queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup
core.when: the planner decides whether to batch or fuse it
core.then: combine compatible calls or computations to amortize I/O, setup, serialization or scheduling overhead only without changing accepted logical results, preserving item identity, failure independence, transaction/authority boundaries, order and resource limits.
prefer: Keep batching internal to a product capability (the normal case); no journey or flow router schema change is needed.
Write acceptances for mixed outcomes, batch boundaries, item-result mapping and equivalence; measure throughput and tail latency.
avoid: Fusing across product capability ownership merely to reduce calls.
Batches that lose per-item results, couple failures, cross transaction boundaries or reorder items.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior from this pattern, or treating it as a new runtime dispatch option.
Treating this advisory guidance as independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators still apply.
core.why: Batching amortizes per-call overhead but helps only if callers keep the same per-item results and isolation.
evidence: Tests cover mixed success/failure outcomes, batch-size boundaries, item-to-result mapping, and equivalence with unbatched results.
Throughput and tail latency are measured for the batched path.
The batching normally stays internal to a product capability, with no journey or flow router schema change. Reducing calls alone does not justify fusion across product capability ownership.
Existing plan and source validators apply.
verification: Guidance for agents, not independent enforcement and not a new runtime dispatch option; the existing plan and source validators still apply.
Unimplemented orchestration behavior cannot be inferred from a pattern.

values: repeated homogeneous operations, database queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup

fires: A plan or product capability contains repeated homogeneous calls, database queries or repeated setup that could be combined to amortize I/O, setup, serialization or scheduling overhead, even before anyone proposes batching.
A plan contains vectorizable computation that could be fused, even before anyone proposes fusion.
A plan proposes fusing vectorizable computations.
A DESIRED OUTCOME or acceptance is being written for a batched or fused path inside a product capability, or an agent is implementing one.

A plan or request relies on orchestration or runtime behavior that is not implemented (such as batch dispatch, scheduling or retries) and justifies it by citing this pattern. The rule fires to apply the caution that such behavior cannot be inferred.
doesNotFire: Single, non-repeated operations with no overhead to amortize.
Work with no repeated homogeneous operations, queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup.

neutralityNotes: This planning-pattern convention is method-level in its canonical source, so the core is essentially the Bun text unchanged: it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, and nothing in it needs concrete profile data (no paths, suffixes, idioms or tool names), hence profileRequirements is empty and no keys are proposed. The artifact words the core keeps - product capability, journey, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance - are ATDD-method structure concepts canonized in the closed vocabulary (urn.capability, urn.journey, urn.desired-outcome, urn.acceptance, layout.capability_dir, roles.plan_artifact.kinds), not Bun realization details, so they are not bunOnly; 'flow router schema' likewise appears verbatim in the canonical source and names no stack, so it was kept rather than inventing a profile key for it. 'Runtime dispatch option' and 'orchestration' refer to the product's runtime behavior, not to any stack runtime. Per-rule severity (3) and the advisory disposition, the not-independent-enforcement scope, and the orchestration-inference caution live in core:verification. The fact notes of bun.json are dropped because the neutral fact schema has no note field; their substance survives as the observability values and the fires situations. bunOnly is empty because every agent-facing item has a stack-neutral equivalent; the Bun sidecar's remaining realization metadata (rule_id planner.journey.strategy.batched, source path/sha, audit, additions, trace) sits outside the item numbering and stays with bun.json.
